ext.getStarted.faq.title: FAQ
ext.getStarted.faq.configure.q: llmar configure says “~/.config is writable by others without the sticky bit”
ext.getStarted.faq.configure.a: Ubuntu's default umask makes ~/.config group-writable. Current llmar accepts that when the group is your own private group. With an older copy, run this (or set LLMAR_CONFIG_DIR, and set it for Claude Code and Codex too):
ext.getStarted.faq.redirectPort.q: What goes in redirect_port in the Codex config?
ext.getStarted.faq.redirectPort.a: This page fills it in: it is the loopback port Codex listens on for its own sign-in ({port}), registered for this deployment. Keep it as shown.
ext.getStarted.faq.gatewaySignIn.q: Codex: “Gateway sign-in required or unavailable” after signing in
ext.getStarted.faq.gatewaySignIn.a: Codex could not store its sign-in: Linux without a keyring (servers, SSH sessions). Uncomment this line in the gateway_oauth table, start Codex and sign in again. The sign-in then lives in $CODEX_HOME/secrets/gateway_oauth.json (mode 0600).
ext.getStarted.faq.ssh.q: Signing in on a remote machine over SSH
ext.getStarted.faq.ssh.a: Both sign-ins return to 127.0.0.1 on the machine that runs the tool. Forward the callback ports when you connect, then open the printed sign-in URL on your own computer (llmar login --no-browser prints it).
ext.getStarted.faq.path.q: Why an absolute path to llmar-token in the Codex config?
ext.getStarted.faq.path.a: Codex does not expand ~. Put your login name in place of <you>, or run this after saving the file:
ext.getStarted.faq.status2.a: llmar has no valid sign-in. Run llmar-token in a terminal to see why; usually you run llmar login again (every {refreshDays} days, or after an admin disabled and re-enabled you).
ext.getStarted.faq.maxTokens.a: That works. GPT models on Bedrock reject max_tokens, so the router renames it to max_completion_tokens when a GPT model serves the request. Other models get the request unchanged.
ext.getStarted.faq.whichModel.a: Every response carries x-router-model (the model that served it) and x-router-decision. The Decisions page lists each request with its basis.
ext.getStarted.faq.metadata.q: Codex warns “Model metadata for 'auto' not found”
ext.getStarted.faq.metadata.a: Harmless: auto is the router's alias, not a model Codex knows. That is why the context window is set in the config.
ext.getStarted.faq.codexPin.q: Codex: a 400 pin-not-allowed on the Decisions page while the session works
ext.getStarted.faq.codexPin.a: Some Codex background passes name a model of their own instead of auto, such as memory extraction at startup (gpt-6-luna). The router refuses a name that is neither an alias nor an allowed model, so only that pass fails; your conversation is not affected. Keep this table in config.toml (it is in the snippet above), or set generate_memories = false there to turn memories off. An admin can instead add the name as an alias on the Routing policy page.
ext.getStarted.faq.claudeBedrock.q: Claude Code shows “Amazon Bedrock” in its header, or “The provided model identifier is invalid”
ext.getStarted.faq.claudeBedrock.a: Claude Code is calling Bedrock directly: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK is set in your environment or in another settings file, and it wins over ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Keep "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK": "0" in the router settings (it is in the snippet above), restart Claude Code and check that the header no longer says Amazon Bedrock. To see what is set:
ext.getStarted.faq.claudeApiKey.q: Claude Code warns “Both apiKeyHelper and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set”
ext.getStarted.faq.claudeApiKey.a: An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your environment takes the place of apiKeyHelper, so the router never gets your llmar token. Unset it for router sessions and remove it from your settings files:
ext.getStarted.faq.claudeModel.q: Claude Code: “Model "auto" isn't recognized · context assumed to be 200k tokens”
ext.getStarted.faq.claudeModel.a: Claude Code does not know the router's alias auto, so it assumes a 200K context window and compacts the conversation at 200K. The router's Claude models have a 1M window. Keep this line in the env block of the router settings (it is in the snippet above) and restart Claude Code. Use a smaller value only if your admin limits you to a model with a smaller window.
ext.getStarted.faq.expired403.q: Claude Code: “Please run /login · API Error: 403 insufficient_scope” in the middle of a session
ext.getStarted.faq.expired403.a: Not a permission problem and not an Anthropic sign-in: the gateway answers an expired access token with 403 insufficient_scope. Don't run /login; send the prompt again. llmar hands out a new token when the same token is asked for again right away.
